children: 0939 ET - Investors are increasingly pricing in the possibility of the Bank of England raising interest rates in the coming months due to inflation concerns as oil prices rise. Markets fully price in one quarter-point BOE rate increase by December, and a second rate hike by March 2027, LSEG data show. Brent crude price rises 1.1% to $97.39 per barrel. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0925 ET - Global markets could face increased volatility due to rising geopolitical tensions, uncertainty around the U.S. midterm elections and an unclear outlook on U.S. interest rates, Validus Risk Management's Kambiz Kazemi says in a note. Renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities have caused oil prices to rise and weakened risk appetite. "Monetary policy uncertainty, political risk and geopolitical tension" could drive volatility across asset classes, he says. Ten-year gilt yields rise 1.9 basis points to last trade at 5.158% and ten-year Bund yields climb 2.8 basis points to 3.369%, Tradeweb data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0756 ET - Monetary policy expectations were the main drivers of government bond yield rises in much of August, Fidelity International's Marion Le Morhedec says in a note. Two-year U.S. Treasury yields rose and 30-year yields fell slightly, flattening the curve as markets reassessed the Federal Reserve's reaction function, the global fixed income CIO says. "Jackson Hole reinforced that move, with Chairman Kevin Warsh reiterating the U.S. Federal Reserve's commitment to its 2% inflation target and markets increasing the probability of a September hike to around 60%, she says. More recently longer-dated yields have joined the selloff, suggesting a broad reassessment by investors of the term premium--the additional compensation investors demand for buying long-dated bonds--, she says. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0752 ET - Investors are looking ahead to U.S. inflation data due to be released on Friday for clues on the possible path of U.S. Federal Reserve rate decisions. Last week's U.S. jobs data came in stronger-than-expected, leading markets to price in an increased chance of the Fed increasing interest rates in September. "A hot inflation report on the back of the strong jobs data would likely tip the balance in favour of a hike, while any moderation in core CPI would push back bets to December," XM's Raffi Boyadjian says in a note. Markets price in a 57% chance of a Fed rate increase in September, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0743 ET - Fitch Ratings affirmed Qatar at AA with a negative outlook as risks from the U.S.-Iran war continue to weigh on the sovereign's fiscal and debt profile. Fitch now forecasts Qatar's economy to contract 18.8% in 2026, with the general-government deficit at 2.7% of GDP and debt rising to 64.1% of GDP, before growth rebounds 16% in 2027. The rating committee highlighted risks of further damage to hydrocarbon infrastructure, uncertainty over LNG transit through the Strait of Hormuz and the conflict's impact on fiscal accounts, reserves and Qatar Investment Authority assets. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

0725 ET - German industry got off to a weak start in the third quarter, even though the decline may primarily attributable to a one-time effect in auto production, Commerzbank economist Ralph Solveen says in a note. Output fell 1.1% in July, with a temporary stoppage to retool a car plant for e-vehicle manufacturing driving a 9.2% drop in car production, data agency Destatis said. "However, even without this effect, production would continue to trend downward," Solveen says. With low water levels on German rivers also hampering production in August, the German economy is likely to expand at a slower pace in the third quarter than it did in previous quarters, he says. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)

0711 ET - Global credit risks are increasingly being shaped by the prospect of an AI-driven market correction and persistent Middle East geopolitical uncertainty affecting funding conditions, Fitch Ratings says. Credit resilience remains, but slowing U.S. consumer momentum, inflation risks and fiscal constraints could amplify shocks and pressure credit quality, the ratings firm says. Global bond yields have climbed as renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities lift oil prices and increase inflation concerns, with the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield recently reaching its highest level since 2023. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

0652 ET - Yields on U.K. 30-year government bonds, or gilts, rise modestly as investors await a potential long-dated gilt syndication this week. The Debt Management Office announced plans to sell January 2056 gilt via syndication in the week starting September 7, subject to demand and market conditions. The DMO also plans to sell 5 billion pounds in a new May 2030 gilt through an auction on Thursday. Thirty-year gilt yields climb 0.4 basis point to last trade at 5.785%, Tradeweb data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0650 ET - John Healey's first speech as U.K. treasury chief gave little away ahead of his first budget on Oct. 28, focusing mainly on growing business investment, Kathleen Brooks at XTB says in a note. "This is one way to boost public sector spending without adding pressure to the national debt, since this spending is outside of Healey's fiscal rules," she says. Healey also reiterated plans for fiscal devolution, which could include a portion of income tax, though details were lacking, Brooks adds. Healey didn't rule out tax increases, which could suggest that taxes will be raised. "However, we think that the fact he is talking about growth... suggests that tax rises in this budget would not help him to reach his mission." (don.forbes@wsj.com)

0635 ET - Markets have gone too far in pricing interest-rate rises by the European Central Bank, Generali Investments' Florian Spaete says in a note. Eurozone money markets currently fully price in a 25 basis-point rate hike this week and two further increases through 2027, LSEG data show. Beyond September, Generali Investments expects only one additional hike in the fourth quarter, however. It considers that second-round inflation effects or accelerating wage pressure remain limited. Still, this doesn't mean Bund yields have scope to fall meaningfully near term as any correction in rate expectations is likely to be offset by higher risk premia, the senior bond strategist says. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0634 ET - Sterling rises slightly while gilt yields trim an earlier rise after U.K. Treasury Chief John Healey pledged government plans to drive economic growth. Healey delivered his first speech as the Treasury Chief at a manufacturing facility in Coventry on Monday. Healey said that delivering economic growth was the first priority of this government. He also announced a 150 million pounds fund from the British Business Bank for fast-growing firms in the North of England. Sterling rises 0.1% to $1.3534. The euro weakens by 0.1% to 0.8583 pounds. Ten-year gilt yields trade steady on the day at 5.140%, having traded up more than 2 basis points in early trade. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0617 ET - The 1.1% drop in German industrial output in July defies the solid order intake and noticeable recent improvement in business sentiment, KfW chief economist Dirk Schumacher says. "The decline in industrial production can therefore be explained primarily by production changes in the automotive industry," he says. German data agency Destatis noted that a multi-week shutdown at a car plant was likely one of the main drivers of the fall. In August and September, the low water levels of the Rhine likely further dampened production, Schumacher says. However, the signals from orders and sentiment indicators point to the underlying improving trend, even if that will probably only be reflected in the figures for the fourth quarter, he says. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)
